1.w: Now the Pharisees and some of the experts in the law who came from Jerusalem gathered around him.

2.w: And they saw that some of Jesus’ disciples ate their bread with unclean hands, that is, unwashed.

3.w: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they perform a ritual washing, holding fast to the tradition of the elders.

4.w: And when they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash. They hold fast to many other traditions: the washing of cups, pots, kettles, and dining couches.)

5.w: The Pharisees and the experts in the law asked him, “Why do your disciples not live according to the tradition of the elders, but eat with unwashed hands?”

6.w: He said to them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: “‘This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.

7.w: They worship me in vain, teaching as doctrine the commandments of men.’

8.w: Having no regard for the command of God, you hold fast to human tradition.”

9.w: He also said to them, “You neatly reject the commandment of God in order to set up your tradition.

10.w: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever insults his father or mother must be put to death.’

11.w: But you say that if anyone tells his father or mother, ‘Whatever help you would have received from me is corban’ (that is, a gift for God),

12.w: then you no longer permit him to do anything for his father or mother.

13.w: Thus you nullify the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many things like this.”

14.w: Then he called the crowd again and said to them, “Listen to me, everyone, and understand.

15.w: There is nothing outside of a person that can defile him by going into him. Rather, it is what comes out of a person that defiles him.”

17.w: Now when Jesus had left the crowd and entered the house, his disciples asked him about the parable.

18.w: He said to them, “Are you so foolish? Don’t you understand that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile him?

19.w: For it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and then goes out into the sewer.” (This means all foods are clean.)

20.w: He said, “What comes out of a person defiles him.

21.w: For from within, out of the human heart, come evil ideas, sexual immorality, theft, murder,

22.w: adultery, greed, evil, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, pride, and folly.

23.w: All these evils come from within and defile a person.”

24.w: After Jesus left there, he went to the region of Tyre. When he went into a house, he did not want anyone to know, but he was not able to escape notice.

25.w: Instead, a woman whose young daughter had an unclean spirit immediately heard about him and came and fell at his feet.

26.w: The woman was a Greek, of Syrophoenician origin. She asked him to cast the demon out of her daughter.

27.w: He said to her, “Let the children be satisfied first, for it is not right to take the children’s bread and to throw it to the dogs.”

28.w: She answered, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

29.w: Then he said to her, “Because you said this, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”

30.w: She went home and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.

31.w: Then Jesus went out again from the region of Tyre and came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee in the region of the Decapolis.

32.w: They brought to him a deaf man who had difficulty speaking, and they asked him to place his hands on him.

33.w: After Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, he put his fingers in the man’s ears, and after spitting, he touched his tongue.

34.w: Then he looked up to heaven and said with a sigh, “Ephphatha” (that is, “Be opened”).

35.w: And immediately the man’s ears were opened, his tongue loosened, and he spoke plainly.

36.w: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But as much as he ordered them not to do this, they proclaimed it all the more.

37.w: People were completely astounded and said, “He has done everything well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”
